correctness.rationale: The exact domain is the real scalar plus countable ℓ_1 with any normalized absolute two-variable lattice norm. The ordinary ℓ_1 lattice isomorphism has norm K_ν and inverse norm one, giving an upper projectivity bound via de Pagter--Wickstead Theorem 11.8. The separable Banach lattice B=c⊕c_0 with norm sup_n(|u_n|+|v_n|) and finite-coordinate ideals has quotient isometrically ℝ⊕∞c_0. The contraction T(a,x)=(a,ιx) has norm one; positivity and coordinate-n invariance for n>m force every stagewise lattice lift to have norm ≥(s+t)/ν(s,t). Maximizing gives K_ν. The explicit lift S_0(a,x)=(constant a,ιx) has norm K_ν, so this lower bound is attained at every stage. Semiprojectivity is equivalent to K_ν=1, which forces ν=ℓ_1². All positive parameters, zero cases, q=∞ endpoint and nonsymmetric norms are covered. No numerics substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: An exact, geometrically natural infinite-dimensional projectivity invariant is classified for the full family of normalized absolute scalar–ℓ_1 sums. It resolves the full sum-norm boundary between the positive ℓ_1 permanence and the negative max-sum example in the recent semiprojectivity paper. A single explicit separable quotient tower measures and attains every lifting loss, not merely a negative existential result. Every constant from 1 to 2 occurs and arbitrarily small lattice renormings can destroy semiprojectivity. Although the proof is brief and adapted from the source, the classification and sharp stagewise constant are natural structural quantities, not arbitrary parameter substitutions or a table recomputation.
